newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia rightist party office hit by blast.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia rightist party office hit by blast.

text.p: Unknown attackers hurled an explosive device into the offices of a Slovenian rightwing political party on Monday, causing damage but injuring no one, police said.
The attack on the minority Republican Union party in the town of Velenje, 100 km (60 miles) east of Ljubljana, came just six days before the country's general election.
"It is too early to say whether the motive was political but that might be the case due to its timing," police spokesman Miran Koren told Reuters by telephone.
He said the device was thrown through a first floor window. The blast caused damage inside the office but two party workers in an adjoining room were unhurt.

The Republican Union is one of 28 political parties competing in the former Yugoslav republic's general election on Sunday. Opinion polls show the tiny Republican Union unlikely to muster more than a handful of votes.
The explosion was the third in the Velenje area this year and four other unexploded devices have been found by police.
